preamble: No documented sound change from the voiceless uvular stop [q] to the voiced alveolar stop [d] has been found. The previous claim of a regular Hebrew q > d shift is unfounded: Hebrew ק continues Proto-Semitic *q (emphatic *ḳ) unchanged in place, and the well-known Semitic correspondences involving q (Aramaic q for Proto-Semitic *ṣ́, as in Aramaic ʔarqā vs Hebrew ʔereṣ 'earth') run from a lateral emphatic toward q, not from q to d.

examples.note: No Hebrew word shows q > d; the entry is kept only to record the misattribution.

sources: Blau, J. (2010). Phonology and Morphology of Biblical Hebrew. Eisenbrauns. https://doi.org/10.1515/9781575066011
